disclaimer: Injury and roster statuses reflect reports as of the evening of Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. NFL.com's Week 1 injury page still lists every team as "No Injuries Reported" - official Week 1 injury reports are not due until Wednesday, Sept. 9 - so everything here comes from beat and insider reporting rather than league filings. New in this update: Bears RB D'Andre Swift's Thursday exit has been resolved - Adam Schefter reported Friday that sources described it as "a cramp" rather than the midsection injury initially feared, and he is upgraded to active and expected back at practice before the Sept. 13 opener; Bears WR Rome Odunze likewise "should be all good" after limping off Thursday, though Chicago is cautious given last year's right-foot stress fracture. Colts WR Alec Pierce has been added - Indianapolis activated him off the active/PUP list Thursday, Sept. 3 after offseason ankle surgery and he was a full participant in Thursday's practice, with Pierce calling Week 1 at Baltimore "the goal." Giants WR Malik Nabers has shed his red non-contact jersey and been cleared for full contact (Harbaugh: "probably moving the best we've seen him look"), but sat out Friday's preseason game and stayed noncommittal on the Sept. 13 opener. Carried over: Cardinals RB James Conner is on injured reserve with a return designation (ankle), first eligible in Week 5 at Detroit, and Arizona waived RB Trey Benson in late August. 49ers DE Sam Okuayinonu (foot) did not fly to Melbourne and is questionable for the opener, while Edge Nick Bosa and TE George Kittle both made the trip and are trending toward playing. Commanders Edge Odafe Oweh (calf) is expected back at practice next week though HC Dan Quinn called his Week 1 availability unclear. Buccaneers WRs Jalen McMillan (knee) and Emeka Egbuka (toe) are both "headed in the right direction" for Sept. 13, per HC Todd Bowles. Bears RB Kyle Monangai remains week-to-week with a hyperextended knee. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike has begun taking part in team drills and is day-to-day; Ravens WR Zay Flowers is back at practice and expected to play Sept. 13. Bengals WRs Ja'Marr Chase (left knee) and Tee Higgins (heel contusion) did no work this week, though HC Zac Taylor said earlier in the week he felt good about Chase's availability; Cincinnati returns Monday, Sept. 7. Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (right ankle) has not practiced since Aug. 24 but is expected to be ready for the Sept. 9 opener at Seattle. Texans RT Braden Smith is on IR with a partially torn plantar fascia. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes is a full participant off Dec. 2025 ACL/LCL surgery. Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) remains "on the mend" but HC Klint Kubiak is optimistic for Week 1. Rams Edge Myles Garrett has not practiced since early August with knee swelling (McVay relayed a self-assessed '85%'), though there is no indication he is at risk of missing the opener. Lions safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are on reserve/PUP for four games; Broncos Edge Jonathon Cooper and Packers RB Josh Jacobs are on the Commissioner's Exempt List; Packers Edge Micah Parsons is on reserve/PUP; Saints RB Alvin Kamara (MCL) is out at least a month; Raiders rookie Edge Keyron Crawford is out for the season with an Achilles injury. Some depth/practice-squad entries may lag the transaction wire. Impact scores are editorial estimates, not official ratings.

injury.note: Slipped and hurt his lower right ankle at practice on Aug. 24 and has not practiced since. He was again absent from the media-access portion of practice Thursday, Sept. 3, per Mike Reiss of ESPN, extending the streak through New England's Seattle prep week. He has been seen in the locker room walking without a limp, and the Boston Globe has reported he should be "good to go" for the Sept. 9 opener at Seattle, though he has not been cleared to participate. Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the alternatives.
Passed his physical and was activated off the PUP list; practiced Aug. 10 for the first time this camp. On track to start at safety in Seattle's Sept. 9 season opener vs. New England.

Charbonnet tore his ACL in the playoff loss to San Francisco and had surgery in February. Seattle opened camp by placing him on the PUP list July 24, and reporting points to a return around midseason rather than Week 1.

Broke his ankle on Seattle's first defensive snap of the Aug. 23 preseason game at Tennessee and was carted off in an air cast. HC Mike Macdonald said Clark will be out multiple months; the Seahawks placed him on injured reserve Aug. 25 along with OL Mason Richman. The second-round rookie out of TCU had been pushing for the starting free safety job and a significant defensive role.
ir
The Seahawks placed Bobo (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.

The 49ers held McCaffrey out for roughly two weeks in August; he and HC Kyle Shanahan both said it was planned load management plus calf tightness after his 413-touch 2025 season, not a new injury. He practiced Tuesday, Sept. 1 and is back to full participation in regular team drills with no setbacks, and is expected to play in the Sept. 10 opener vs. the Rams in Melbourne.

Activated off PUP on Aug. 23 after rupturing his Achilles on Jan. 11 in the playoff win at Philadelphia - back on the field in under eight months. Per the AP he practiced three straight days through Wednesday, Sept. 2 and appears ready to try to play in Week 1; he traveled to Australia after those sessions. GM John Lynch said Kittle has "absolutely crushed" his objective return benchmarks. He has not been formally cleared, so he remains day-to-day.

GM John Lynch announced Pearsall will have surgery on his PCL and is out for the entire 2026 season; placed on injured reserve. Recurring swelling in the same knee had limited him to two camp practices. 49ers re-signed Deebo Samuel in response.

injury.type: Groin strain (also missed time with a quad strain)
injury.note: Missed practice Aug. 31 and Sept. 1, and GM John Lynch said Tuesday that Evans would likely not practice until the team reached Australia. Evans beat that timeline, returning to the practice field Wednesday, Sept. 2 before the flight. He remains day-to-day, but the 49ers expect him to play in Week 1 vs. the Rams.

injury.type: Knee soreness / tendinitis (surgically repaired right knee)
injury.note: Had not practiced since Aug. 3 with soreness and tendinitis in the right knee repaired after his 2025 ACL tear. Bosa returned to practice Wednesday, Sept. 2 - his first session in nearly a month - and got through team work before the 49ers flew to Australia that night. He said afterward he believes he will play the opener: "Take it one day at a time but today was a great day." San Francisco has not formally cleared him or ruled him out, so he stays day-to-day.
Kirk (calf) was placed on injured reserve by the 49ers on Sunday with a designation to return.

Did not board the 49ers' charter to Melbourne on Wednesday, Sept. 2, staying back in the U.S. to continue treating a foot injury. NFL.com listed him as questionable for the Week 1 game against the Rams; with the team already overseas, his participation would require a late trip.

Left the joint practice with Dallas and missed much of the last two weeks of camp with what Sean McVay described as soreness in the psoas. Nacua returned to practice Sunday, Aug. 30 and is not considered in danger of missing regular-season time; he is expected to be ready for the Sept. 10 opener vs. San Francisco in Melbourne.

Garrett has missed roughly a dozen straight practices with what the Rams describe as minor swelling in the knee, including the joint work with Dallas and the Aug. 25 session - the 12th he sat out. HC Sean McVay put him at about '85%' and said the club is deliberately erring on the side of caution with its new star edge rusher: 'The goal is, what can we do to be able to get him ready to roll for Australia?' - a reference to the Sept. 10 opener vs. the 49ers in Melbourne. He has been on the field in street clothes working with trainers on the side. The Rams gave players Tuesday through Thursday off and return to practice Friday, Sept. 4, which is the next real read on his availability. No structural diagnosis has been made public.

Odunze limped off with trainers during Thursday's final preseason practice, but reporting Friday indicated he "should be all good" and avoided a serious setback. Chicago is being cautious given the right-foot stress fracture that bothered him for much of last season; he is expected back at practice before Sept. 13.

Swift left Thursday's practice holding his midsection after a goal-line carry and was described as being in significant discomfort, but Adam Schefter reported Friday that sources characterized it as "a cramp." He is expected back at practice before the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina.

injury.type: Hyperextended left knee, bone bruise, small fracture - underwent surgery
injury.note: HC Ben Johnson announced Aug. 11 that Bryant underwent knee surgery and will now miss 4-6 months, a significant setback from the initial 8-10 week outlook (surgery wasn't originally expected). Bears remain hopeful he could be available if Chicago makes the playoffs. Was Chicago's marquee free-agent addition this offseason (3-year, $40M deal).

Opened training camp on the PUP list with a calf injury that also sidelined him for OTAs and minicamp. GM Ryan Poles said Aug. 6 there's been a frustrating 'delay' in his recovery with no firm return timetable; Gordon says he believes he'll be ready soon.

Hurt getting tangled up with CB Tyrique Stevenson on the final rep of red-zone one-on-ones. Expected to miss the rest of the preseason (about a month) but the Bears believe he'll be ready for the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina. Poised for a bigger role after the DJ Moore trade to Buffalo; caught 47 passes for 652 yards and 2 TDs as a rookie in 2025.

Hurt getting tangled up with DT Grady Jarrett during an Aug. 16 practice. Initial tests suggested the knee was structurally sound, but a follow-up MRI confirmed the hyperextension. HC Ben Johnson said this week that Monangai remains "week-to-week," per Chris Emma, leaving Week 1 in doubt. He was in line for a bigger role behind the injury-prone D'Andre Swift.

injury.type: Ruptured patellar tendon (right knee) - surgically repaired
injury.note: Suffered in the Panthers' January playoff loss to the Rams; underwent surgery to repair the tendon. Rehab is reportedly "ahead of schedule" and the Panthers are "really feeling good" about his progress, per team reporting. On PUP to open camp; GM Dan Morgan remains optimistic he can return at some point this season.
Non-contact tear suffered on the first day of training camp practice — out for the season. The injury happened during the mandatory acclimation period, which the NFLPA is investigating.

Diagnosed with a blood clot in his lung in late June and placed on the reserve/non-football injury (NFI) list; immediately started on blood thinners and is reportedly responding well to treatment. Expected to miss the start of the regular season, per ESPN, though the team believes he could return at some point during the year.

Strained the hamstring in one-on-ones in mid-August and has not played in a preseason game. HC Dave Canales said Monday, Aug. 24 that Hubbard is expected to be ready for Week 1, though Carolina isn't rushing him back. Backup Jonathon Brooks has seen expanded preseason reps in the meantime.

Missed time late in training camp with a toe issue that Tampa Bay flagged as a factor in its Week 1 roster construction. The team has said it expects Egbuka back before Week 1 and at full strength, and he was kept on the initial 53-man roster. No specific return-to-practice date has been reported.

HC Todd Bowles said Wednesday, Sept. 2 that McMillan (knee) and Emeka Egbuka (toe) are both "headed in the right direction" for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Cincinnati. No return-to-practice date has been announced and Tampa Bay's first official injury report is not due until Wednesday, Sept. 9.

Hyperextended the left knee landing awkwardly on a catch at the Aug. 25 practice; he called it "just a little tweak" but the issue has lingered. HC Zac Taylor said Tuesday, Sept. 1 that Chase would be limited all week while adding he expects him to "be good at the end of the week." In practice, Chase ended up doing no work at all: he was present but not suited up Wednesday, Sept. 2 (per Gabi Sorrentino of Fox 19 Cincinnati) and did not work again at Thursday's (Sept. 3) walkthrough-style session, per Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. Cincinnati then broke for the weekend and returns Monday, Sept. 7 to begin true game-week prep for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Tampa Bay. Taylor has continued to voice optimism for the opener; no official diagnosis has been issued.

HC Zac Taylor disclosed Tuesday, Sept. 1 that Higgins is dealing with a heel contusion and would be limited in practice alongside Ja'Marr Chase, saying he expects both receivers "will be good at the end of the week." Higgins did not take part at all Wednesday, Sept. 2 (per Ben Baby of ESPN) and did not work again Thursday, Sept. 3, per Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com - so he missed the entire mock game week. The Bengals broke for the weekend and return Monday, Sept. 7 to prepare for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Tampa Bay, where Taylor still expects him available.

Carted off during Cincinnati's first padded/11-on-11 practice with a hyperextended knee; follow-up testing showed no ligament damage. Coach Zac Taylor confirmed Aug. 7 he'll be out 'several weeks' but is expected back well before the regular season ends.

MRI results (Aug. 19) confirmed a sprained MCL after Kamara left Tuesday's joint practice vs. Dallas; he avoided a more serious structural tear. Expected to be sidelined at least a month, which would put his return around mid-to-late September - likely missing the Sept. 13 opener at San Francisco and possibly Week 2 as well.

Hurt in the preseason game vs. the Rams; HC Kellen Moore confirmed Tuesday, Aug. 25 that Chandler will miss the entire season, and New Orleans placed him (along with TE Moliki Matavao) on season-ending injured reserve. Compounds a thin backfield with Alvin Kamara out (MCL) and Devin Neal dealing with a hamstring - the Saints traded for RB Zamir White this week in response.

Bresee tore his ACL in an early training-camp practice and was placed on injured reserve Aug. 7 ahead of surgery. He is out for 2026 and targeting full health for 2027; John Ridgeway is expected to start in his place.
Tyson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return by New Orleans on Sunday.
Tipton (leg) is expected to begin the 2026 regular season on the reserve/PUP list, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.

Took a hit to the hip in an Aug. 17 scrimmage and was rested while it calmed down; HC Dan Campbell would not guarantee Week 1, saying "I feel like we'll be OK, but I don't know." LaPorta returned to practice Tuesday, Aug. 25, taking part in both individual and team drills - a strong sign for the Sept. 13 opener vs. New Orleans, though Detroit has not committed and is expected to stay cautious. He is separately fully cleared from November 2025 back surgery.

Still recovering from the Achilles tear he suffered in the first week of December 2025. Detroit placed him on the reserve/PUP list at Sunday's (Aug. 30) cutdown, so he is ineligible for the first four games. With Kerby Joseph also on reserve/PUP, the Lions open the season without both starting safeties.

Detroit placed Joseph on the reserve/PUP list at Sunday's (Aug. 30) cutdown, which rules the All-Pro safety out of at least the first four games. He has been unable to shake a knee injury carried over from last season. He does not count against the 53-man roster while on reserve/PUP.
ir
The Lions placed Pacheco (back) on injured reserve Tuesday.
Shavers (knee) was moved to the reserve/PUP list by the Bills on Sunday.

Suffered a season-ending torn ACL during Tuesday's joint practice with the Raiders, falling awkwardly on a red-zone route in 11-on-11 drills. The 2025 second-round pick started 10 games as a rookie (525 yards, 6 TDs); Houston will lean more on Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel in his absence.
The Texans placed Horton (Achilles) on injured reserve Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

Held out of practice in late August with what HC DeMeco Ryans called a lower leg injury - "We expect him back soon." Clowney re-signed with Houston in early August for a second stint with the team that drafted him No. 1 overall in 2014. No firm return date, but the team's public tone points to a short-term absence.

injury.type: Partially torn plantar fascia (foot) - on injured reserve, designated to return
injury.note: Carted off the Aug. 26 joint practice with Carolina; Adam Schefter reported the next day that Smith injured his plantar fascia. The diagnosis is a partial tear with a four-to-six-week recovery window, and Houston placed Smith on injured reserve as a designated-to-return player alongside fellow T Sam Hagen, per Pro Football Rumors - which rules him out for at least the first four games. GM Nick Caserio confirmed the four-to-six-week timeline. Trent Brown, who had been competing with Smith, takes over as the starting right tackle.
ir

injury.type: Left leg injury (no structural damage) - recovered
injury.note: Returned to full practice and 11-on-11 team drills Monday, Aug. 17, after missing most of the prior week following a leg injury suffered tangling feet with WR Ja'Kobi Lane. HC Jesse Minter called the return a positive sign; Wiggins is set to be available for joint practices with Minnesota later this week.

Returned to full practice and 11-on-11 team drills Monday, Aug. 17, after a groin issue sidelined him for several days. HC Jesse Minter said Humphrey bounced back well; on track for Baltimore's joint practices with Minnesota later this week.

Tore the patellar tendon during the Aug. 19 joint practice with the Vikings in Eagan, Minnesota, and was carted off in a full-leg brace. Baltimore placed him on injured reserve Wednesday, Aug. 26, ending his season. He had been taking most first-team center reps after Tyler Linderbaum's offseason move to the Raiders; Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn are the leading options to replace him.

Activated off the reserve list Aug. 27 while working back from an undisclosed lower-body injury. Flowers returned to the practice field Thursday, Sept. 3 - his first practice in two weeks - and the Ravens said WR Devontez Walker was the only player absent that day. HC Jesse Minter said the focus has been on making sure Flowers is ready for Week 1, and he is expected to play the Sept. 13 opener vs. Indianapolis. He also missed time with a quad contusion earlier in August and signed a four-year extension at the start of the month.
ir

Sidelined since Week 2 of last season with a cervical neck injury that put his 2026 return in doubt. He has now begun participating in team drills and is described as day-to-day heading into Week 1. Baltimore did not place him on injured reserve, per Jamison Hensley of ESPN, so he is eligible for the first four games. The two-time Pro Bowler has averaged 6.5 sacks per season over six years.

Left Wednesday's joint practice vs. Atlanta clutching his groin and did not return; HC Shane Steichen confirmed the injury. Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Colts avoided a critical injury — Warren is expected to be out roughly a week, not weeks — though he'll be shut down for the rest of camp/preseason as a precaution. Second-year first-round pick coming off a strong rookie season (76 catches, 817 yards, 5 total TDs) and expected to be a lead target for Daniel Jones; trending toward being ready for the regular season.

Indianapolis activated its No. 1 receiver off the active/PUP list on Thursday, Sept. 3 following offseason ankle surgery. HC Shane Steichen said Pierce was a full participant in Thursday's practice and Pierce said "the goal" is to play in the Week 1 opener at Baltimore; GM Chris Ballard had called it a "hope" earlier in the week.
ir
Originally hurt in an October 2024 collision with Derrick Henry. Placed on reserve/PUP for a second straight season; not expected to play in 2026.
The Browns placed Wright on injured reserve Sunday due to a ruptured Achilles, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
ir

Recovering from Nov. 25, 2025 left-knee ACL surgery (his third career ACL procedure). Cleared Aug. 21 to return to 11-on-11 work but sat out Friday's preseason finale at Miami with only three full practices back. Atlanta's Week 1 depth chart lists Tua Tagovailoa as the starter and omits Penix as an "injured player"; per Ian Rapoport, Tagovailoa inherited the job rather than winning it outright while Penix is not fully cleared. Penix has said full medical clearance could still be a few weeks away, and both QBs are expected to play at some point in 2026.

Carted off during an 11-on-11 period at Tuesday's practice; an MRI later that evening confirmed a torn ACL, per The Athletic's Josh Kendall. The 2025 first-round pick (No. 15 overall) will miss the entire 2026 season.
Atlanta placed Hall on injured reserve Saturday, Aug. 29 as part of its roster reduction. The team has not disclosed the injury.

Activated off the PUP list and returned to practice Monday, Aug. 24, alongside rookie OL Max Iheanachor (neck). HC Mike McCarthy called it a positive step after Ramsey opened camp on PUP with a minicamp knee injury (no surgery required); he's expected to be limited/ramping up gradually. Barring a setback, he's on track to be Pittsburgh's top slot corner for the Sept. 13 regular-season opener vs. Atlanta.

injury.type: Knee injury - reverted to injured reserve
injury.note: Carted off during a non-contact 7-on-7 period at an early padded camp practice. The Steelers waived him with an injury designation; he cleared waivers and reverted to Pittsburgh's injured reserve, likely ending his 2026 season. A 2024 UDFA out of the Bengals' practice squad, he was a depth/roster-bubble receiver - impact score lowered accordingly. Pittsburgh signed WR Jakobie Keeney-James in his place.
Jonathan (thigh) reverted to the Jets' injured reserve Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

Evaluated for a concussion after a hard hit from Bears S Xavier Woods in Thursday's joint practice - a hit HC Robert Saleh called "cheap." Ian Rapoport and follow-up reporting indicate Robinson is not believed to have suffered a concussion and is expected to avoid the protocol; Tennessee is still monitoring him in case symptoms develop.
ir

Rookie first-round pick (No. 3 overall) hurt his ankle late in Arizona's preseason game vs. the Raiders. HC Mike LaFleur said Monday, Aug. 24 that Love is progressing but will be sidelined this week, ruling him out for the rest of the preseason. No long-term prognosis given; the team is still hopeful he's available for the Sept. 13 opener vs. the Chargers.
questionable

injury.type: Ankle - on injured reserve (designated to return)
injury.note: Arizona placed Conner on injured reserve with a designation to return on Aug. 30, per Tom Pelissero, as he continues to recover from the dislocated ankle that ended his 2025 season. He must miss at least the first four games (Chargers, Seahawks, 49ers, Giants) and is first eligible to return in Week 5 at Detroit on Oct. 11. With Trey Benson waived in August, rookie Jeremiyah Love and the remaining backs carry the load until Conner is back.

Returned to practice Saturday, Aug. 22 as a limited participant, per HC Jim Harbaugh - his first practice action since missing 8 straight sessions. Worked through individual drills and the first team-drill period before stepping aside; still considered day-to-day, but the return is a positive sign after a knee flare-up in his surgically repaired patellar tendon. No firm timetable yet for a return to full practice.

Officially placed on season-ending injured reserve Aug. 23 after tearing his ACL when a 49ers defensive lineman fell into his leg during an Aug. 18 joint practice. Signed with the Chargers in March on a 3-year, $30M deal after playing for Washington last season; Chargers will turn to their backup center options for the year.
Campbell (leg) reverted to the Chargers' injured reserve list Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injury.type: Ankle sprain (low-grade; believed more low than high)
injury.note: Helped off the practice field Sunday, Aug. 23 after landing awkwardly on a dive for a catch. Per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter the sprain is believed to be "more low than high" and is not considered long-term; the Raiders did not place him on IR. He did his first on-field work Tuesday, Sept. 1, going through side work with trainers rather than practicing - progress from the previous week, when he was not outside at all. GM John Spytek said Sept. 1 he expects Jeanty "to be back as quick as he can be," while HC Klint Kubiak has stayed noncommittal: "Still on the mend. Still working to get him back." His Week 1 status for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Miami should clarify with the first official injury report on Wednesday, Sept. 9.

The third-round rookie was hurt in the third quarter of the preseason finale vs. the 49ers after being pushed down and landing awkwardly. Initially reported as an ankle injury when Las Vegas placed him on IR at cutdown; HC Klint Kubiak later confirmed it is an Achilles injury that will cost Crawford his entire rookie season.

injury.type: Torn ACL + meniscus repair (left knee) - on reserve/PUP
injury.note: Suffered a torn ACL plus meniscus repair in Week 15 last season vs. Denver. Green Bay made it official with Sunday's cutdown, moving Parsons from active/PUP to reserve/PUP, which rules him out of the first four games (vs. Minnesota, the Jets, Atlanta and Tampa Bay) and makes Week 5 the earliest he can return. Parsons has said his 'most optimistic' target is Week 6 (Oct. 18, SNF vs. his old team the Cowboys at Lambeau), but stressed there's no guarantee given the Packers' internal recovery protocol for ACL-plus injuries.

The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Sunday, Aug. 30, three days after he was formally charged with misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property stemming from an alleged May incident. He is not on Green Bay's 53-man roster and cannot practice or attend games, though he continues to be paid. His initial court appearance is set for Nov. 17, but the league does not have to wait for the legal process to conclude before issuing discipline. The Packers acquired RB Kaleb Johnson from Pittsburgh amid the uncertainty. His earlier August groin strain is no longer the reason for his absence.

New to Green Bay's camp injury report in early August with a sprained foot. Coach Matt LaFleur says he's hopeful Reed will be ready for the Sept. 7 season opener vs. Detroit, though the team is proceeding cautiously with the soft-tissue issue.
The Packers placed Williams (undisclosed) on injured reserve Sunday with a designation to return, Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
Returned to practice July 29 after a mild hamstring strain; fully participated with no limitations in Sunday's (Aug. 9) public training camp practice. On track for Week 1 vs. Chicago.

Adams went down without contact in coverage during the Aug. 15 preseason game at the Giants and was carted off. Testing confirmed a torn right quad tendon and Minnesota placed him on injured reserve Aug. 17, ending his season.
Jefferson (undisclosed) reverted to the Vikings' injured reserve Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
The NFL suspended Jones three games Tuesday for violating the league's substance-abuse policy, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
Fleming (undisclosed) reverted to the Vikings' injured reserve list Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

Hurt in a one-on-one pass-rush rep vs. Odafe Oweh during Saturday's practice; underwent surgery to repair the torn triceps. HC Dan Quinn didn't disclose an exact timeline, but recovery from this type of injury typically runs 4-7 months, likely sidelining him for most if not all of the 2026 season. Washington moved Brandon Coleman to left tackle in his place, with Andrew Wylie as depth; Quinn said the team isn't looking outside the building for additional O-line help.

HC Dan Quinn said Wednesday, Sept. 2 that Oweh is expected to return to practice next week but that his availability for the Sept. 13 opener against the Eagles is unclear. Washington's edge group is already thin, and the defense is counting on him opposite its interior pressure.

Strained lifting weights ahead of camp; placed on PUP list on the first day of training camp. Traded to Philadelphia from Minnesota in April 2026 on a 4-year, $100M deal. DC Vic Fangio said Aug. 11 that Greenard is expected to miss at least a 'couple more weeks,' pushing him past all of training camp, though the injury is still not considered a long-term concern.

Back at practice this week in a limited/individual-drills capacity as the Eagles ramp him up ahead of joint sessions with New England; team says the hamstring issue is not serious and there's no long-term concern, though a firm return-to-full timetable still hasn't been set.
Wilson (knee) reverted to Philadelphia's injured reserve Saturday, per the NFL's transaction log.

Broke his left forearm in Friday's (Aug. 28) preseason game against the Saints, HC Brian Schottenheimer confirmed. Per ESPN, Liufau is scheduled for surgery as early as Monday, Aug. 31, putting the Sept. 13 opener in serious doubt for the third-year linebacker.

Nabers has shed the red non-contact jersey and been cleared for full contact, and HC John Harbaugh said he was "probably moving the best we've seen him look." He did not suit up for Friday's preseason game against the Jets and remains noncommittal about the Sept. 13 opener vs. Dallas, saying his focus is on the full regular season. He is roughly 11 months removed from surgery, at the front edge of the typical 9-12 month ACL window.

Carted off Tuesday's (Aug. 25) practice after his knee buckled running a route; Adam Schefter initially reported a "serious knee injury" and a source confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday, Aug. 26 that it is a torn ACL that will cost him the 2026 season. Austin, 27 and in a contract year, had been in line for a significant role in New York's passing game - a bigger blow with Malik Nabers still working back from his own ACL tear.

Evaluated for a head injury during Friday's (Aug. 28) preseason game vs. the Jets and cleared. HC John Harbaugh said afterward that Tracy has a stinger. No timetable given, but the Giants have not indicated concern for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Dallas.

The NFL placed Cooper on the Commissioner's Exempt List while it reviews domestic-violence charges stemming from two June arrests in Parker, Colo., including a felony second-degree assault by strangulation count. He continues to be paid and may attend meetings and work out at the facility, but cannot practice or attend games. Cooper has posted at least eight sacks in each of the last three seasons (career-high 10.5 in 2024). No return timetable.
ir

Suffered a bruised foot in Friday's (Aug. 28) preseason game against the Vikings, per HC Sean Payton. Mims went to the locker room to be evaluated in the first quarter and did not return. Denver has not given a timetable; the bruise diagnosis points to a short-term issue.

injury.type: Torn ACL + LCL, left knee (surgically repaired) - cleared
injury.note: Tore the ACL and LCL in his left knee in the Dec. 14, 2025 game against the Chargers and had surgery in Dallas performed by Dr. Dan Cooper. Cleared for football activities in July and has not missed a training-camp practice, participating in full; Kansas City held him out of all four preseason games purely as a precaution. Mahomes said Tuesday, Sept. 1 that he feels "great" and is on track to start, and Ian Rapoport reported the same. He is expected to start the Sept. 14 opener vs. Denver.
Smith (undisclosed) reverted to the Chiefs' injured reserve list Monday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
Caldwell (knee) reverted to the Chiefs' injured reserve list Tuesday, Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com reports.
